title: Map analysis steps to explicit rubric anchors
when_to_use: When the task includes a detailed rubric or scoring framework with specific numeric anchors.
experience:
Before executing analysis, scan the rubric for required metrics, calculations, or comparisons.
Create a checklist of every numeric anchor (e.g., baseline values, target thresholds, expected outputs).
Explicitly compute each anchor in your code or query and compare your results to the expected values.
If an anchor cannot be computed, document why and flag the gap as a potential failure point.
Structured your final report sections to match the rubric criteria and explicitly state how each anchor was met.
checklist: Extract all numeric anchors from rubric
common_failure_prevented: Missing required calculations like ROI, retention rates, or crash rates despite the rubric explicitly listing them.

title: Design weighted metrics before segment comparisons
when_to_use: When analyzing performance across heterogeneous groups (e.g., regions, users) where aggregation requires weighting.
experience:
Identify the relevant weight for each entity before calculating group-level averages (e.g., revenue-share, user count, active devices).
Compute weighted versions of key metrics (e.g., weighted retention, weighted revenue, weighted churn).
Compare weighted vs. unweighted results to identify biases.
Use weighted metrics as the primary basis for any segmentation analysis (e.g., high vs. low revenue markets).
Document your weighting rationale and any potential distortions introduced.
checklist: Compute weighted metric for each group
common_failure_prevented: Using simple averages for group comparisons, ignoring that larger markets dominate overall performance.

title: Quantify recommendations with rubric-supplied targets
when_to_use: When providing recommendations based on data and the rubric includes specific improvement targets.
experience:
Extract all recommendation-related numeric targets from the rubric (e.g., increase conversion rate to 0.075, reduce crash rate below 1.8).
For each recommendation, link a concrete action to one or more of these targets.
Define acceptance criteria (e.g., pilot success thresholds, pause rules) using the same targets.
Structure recommendations as: Action → Metric → Current Value → Target Value → Timeline.
If the rubric provides ROI tiers or budget allocations, incorporate them into the prioritization.
common_failure_prevented: Vague suggestions like 'improve quality' without citing specific, rubric-defined KPI targets.
